summary: Phase 0 MCP acceptance harness is correct and complete. All four verify scripts pass (both PASS and FAIL paths). The harness is a pure HTTP client reusing slice1-lab fixture shapes, not the lab binary. All acceptance criteria (A1-A4, L1-L7, S1-S9) are covered. The harness correctly fails against the real production endpoint with the expected Phase 0 baseline violations. No actionable defects found.
follow_up: S9 concurrency-isolation test asserts no calendar-ID overlap between two concurrent clients but does not verify each client sees its own calendars; a server returning empty calendars to both would pass vacuously. Consider asserting each client sees its own subject-bound calendars.

assertNoCalendarLeak (security-isolation.js:285-297) uses a string-matching heuristic (checks for literal "calendars" or "calendar_id" in the body); a production server returning calendar data in a different shape could evade the check. Consider parsing the response body and checking for calendar objects.
important_context: The harness is a regression gate: it stays red (exit 1) against the current production component until later phases implement the MCP lifecycle, public 401 challenge, and authorization-server metadata.
The harness (harness.js/discovery.js/oauth-lifecycle.js/security-isolation.js/lib.js) is a pure HTTP client using only Node built-ins; it does not launch or import the slice1-lab binaries.
The mock servers (mock/server.js, mock/lifecycle-server.js, mock/oauth-provider.js) are verification-only and are not release artifacts.
The Phase 0.4 security harness uses verification-only /_test/* hooks (token mint, grant set/revoke/broaden/reset/delete) on the mock to drive negative-token and grant-state cases in isolation.
The calendar_list permission mapping bug (mcp-server/src/tools/calendar_list.rs:38 checks availability_find instead of calendar_list) is a known Phase 2 fix, not a Phase 0 harness defect.
